units.title: Computer Vision Basics
learn_paragraphs:
Computer Vision helps computers understand images and video.
An image is a grid of pixels. In colour images each pixel has three numbers: Red,
Green and Blue (RGB), each from 0 to 255.
Resolution is the number of pixels, like 1920 × 1080. More pixels show more detail
but need more storage.

new_words.definition: a part that acts, like a motor

computers on the internet that store and process data

units.self_check: I can explain pixels, RGB and resolution.

units.title: Natural Language Processing
learn_paragraphs:
Natural Language Processing (NLP) helps computers understand and produce
human language.
First, text is split into tokens (words or parts of words). Then the AI looks at
patterns.
Sentiment analysis decides if text is positive, negative or neutral. It is used for
reviews and feedback.

units.title: Statistics for AI
learn_paragraphs:
AI relies on statistics to understand data.
Mean = sum ÷ count. Median = middle value after sorting. Mode = most frequent
value.
Range = largest − smallest. These help us describe data and spot unusual values
called outliers.

new_words.definition: the data trail you leave online
a named action, like print()

units.did_you_know: An outlier can pull the mean a lot, but the median hardly moves.
units.think_and_talk: Why might an AI give bad results if its data has many outliers?
units.self_check: I can find mean, median, mode, range and outliers.

units.title: Supervised vs Unsupervised
learn_paragraphs:
In supervised learning, the AI learns from labelled examples, like emails marked
“spam” or “not spam”.
In unsupervised learning, data has no labels. The AI finds groups on its own, called
clustering, like grouping shoppers with similar habits.
A third type, reinforcement learning, learns by trial and error with rewards, like a
game AI.

the middle value

units.did_you_know: Reinforcement learning helped AlphaGo defeat a world champion at the board game Go in 2016.
units.think_and_talk: Which type of learning do you use when you learn to ride a cycle?

units.title: Training Data and Classification
learn_paragraphs:
Classification means putting things into categories, like “ripe” or “unripe” mango.
We split data into a training set (to learn) and a test set (to check). A common split
is 80% train, 20% test.
Good training data is large, balanced (enough of each class) and varied.

units.did_you_know: Engineers never test a model on its training data, because it may have just memorised the answers.

units.title: Python Basics
learn_paragraphs:
Python is the most popular language for AI because it is simple to read.
print() shows output. Variables store values: name = "Asha" . input() takes text
from the user.
Data types: int (whole numbers), float (decimals), str (text), bool (True/False).

units.title: Smart Sensors and IoT
learn_paragraphs:
The Internet of Things (IoT) connects everyday devices to the internet: lights, fans,
meters, watches.
The flow is Sense → Send → Decide → Act. A sensor measures, data goes to the
cloud, AI decides, and a device acts.
Example: a soil moisture sensor tells a smart pump when to water a farm.

units.title: Digital Footprint and Safety
learn_paragraphs:
Your digital footprint is the trail of data you leave online: posts, likes, searches and
location.
Active footprints are things you share on purpose. Passive footprints are collected
without you noticing, like location history.
Protect yourself: strong passwords, two-step verification, think before posting, and
check app permissions.
